title: Finite coefficient change for the dualizing object
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and integers $1\le m\le n$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$ and $B=A_{E,m}$, with their quotient map $A\to B$. Let $a_X:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Work first on the ordinary small etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with derived coefficient extension $T_{A,B}(K)=K\otimes_A^L B$ [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Let $F_{X,A}=Ra_{X,A!}$ be ordinary etale compact support [def-amb-etale-compact-support], let $a_{X,A}^{\times}$ be its right adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and set $\omega_{X,A}=a_{X,A}^{\times}A_s$; use the analogous notation at $B$. Denote the counit at $A_s$ by $\varepsilon_{X,A}:F_{X,A}\omega_{X,A}\to A_s$.

There is a canonical isomorphism
$$
u_{X,A,B}:T_{A,B}\omega_{X,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,B}.
$$
Specifically, let $c_{X,A,B,K}:T_{A,B}F_{X,A}K\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{X,B}T_{A,B}K$ be the compact-support coefficient comparison of [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. Then $u_{X,A,B}$ is the adjoint under $F_{X,B}\dashv a_{X,B}^{\times}$ of
$$
F_{X,B}T_{A,B}\omega_{X,A}\xrightarrow{c_{X,A,B,\omega_{X,A}}^{-1}}T_{A,B}F_{X,A}\omega_{X,A}\xrightarrow{T_{A,B}\varepsilon_{X,A}}T_{A,B}A_s\cong B_s.
$$
In particular its counit identity is
$$
\varepsilon_{X,B}\circ F_{X,B}(u_{X,A,B})=(T_{A,B}\varepsilon_{X,A})\circ c_{X,A,B,\omega_{X,A}}^{-1}.
$$
For $1\le h\le m\le n$ and $C=A_{E,h}$ these isomorphisms satisfy
$$
u_{X,A,C}=u_{X,B,C}\circ T_{B,C}(u_{X,A,B}),\qquad u_{X,A,A}=1,
$$
using the canonical reassociation $T_{B,C}T_{A,B}\cong T_{A,C}$. Their finite pro-etale realization is the same isomorphism after the etale/pro-etale comparison: the dualizing objects are identified by [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison], and the exceptional functor on that constructible realization is the transported functor of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

proof.text: The existence hypotheses are in force. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and itself; hence $s$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X$ and all its finite-type affine charts are Noetherian. By [thm-nagata-compactification], the separated finite-type $a_X$ is compactifiable (the one-point affine base is quasi-compact and quasi-separated). Thus [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] supplies the ordinary etale adjoints at each of $A,B,C$. No adjoint on arbitrary pro-etale sheaves is used.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: scope of the ambient etale adjoint

proof.text:
The constant coefficient sheaf $A_X$ is bounded constructible and has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$: tensor with $A_X$ is the identity. Apply [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] to $K=A_X$. Its dual is $R\mathcal Hom_A(A_X,\omega_{X,A})=\omega_{X,A}$ by evaluation at $1$, so $\omega_{X,A}$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. The same holds for $B$ and $C$. Consequently [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] applies to $K=\omega_{X,A}$. Write $F_R=F_{X,R}$, $T=T_{A,B}$, and $c=c_{X,A,B}$. The adjunction bijection defines one global map $u_{X,A,B}$ with
$$\varepsilon_{X,B}F_B(u_{X,A,B})=(T\varepsilon_{X,A})c_{\omega_{X,A}}^{-1}.$$
This is exactly the displayed definition and counit assertion; existence of a coefficient comparison for an exceptional adjoint has not been assumed.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: finite-Tor domain and construction of the map

proof.text:
We spell out the formal normalization used below. For composable compact-support functors $F_pF_i\cong F_{pi}$ use [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. The composite-adjunction rule [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] says its counit is
$$\varepsilon_{pi}=\varepsilon_p\circ F_p(\varepsilon_i).$$
When the left-functor comparison is available on the whole categories, the comparison with any chosen right adjoint is the counit-compatible unique mate of [lem-trf-adjoint-mate]. For the bounded-below composition comparison, we need only its objectwise version: if $Q_1,Q_2\in D^+$ both represent $L\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(F(L),N)$ for $L\in D^+$, the natural Hom bijections give mutually inverse maps $Q_1\to Q_2$ and $Q_2\to Q_1$ by evaluating on their identities. Naturality says their composites are identities and their transposes are the specified counits. We use this argument only after verifying that both representing objects are bounded below; it requires no composition comparison on unbounded inputs. The coefficient tensor comparisons paste in the same order:
$$c_{pi,K}=F_{p,B}(c_{i,K})\circ c_{p,F_{i,A}K}.$$
This is the normalized coefficient/composition square stated in [lem-sf-compact-coefficient-composition], with the two compact-support composition isomorphisms understood. Its hypotheses hold for the separated finite-type schemes and morphisms used below; its input is finite-Tor constructible by step 2 for the closed factor and by the extension-by-zero check in step 8 for the open factor. The cited statement concerns the actual canonical comparison maps and supplies this equality with the composition identifications. We use the coefficient comparison only in the finite-Tor situations certified in step 2 or in the closed-support assertion below; no claim that $B$ has finite Tor dimension over $A$ is required.

source.place: Proof, second and third paragraphs: normalization of composite adjoints and coefficient maps

proof.text:
For $P=\mathbf A^r_k$ and $p:P\to s$, use the ordinary etale Tate sheaves of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Choose one power $N$ of $\ell$ annihilating $A$ (and hence $B,C$). Its definition $A_P(1)=\mu_{N,P}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A$ gives
$$A_P(r)\otimes_A^L B\cong B_P(r).$$
Indeed the Tate sheaf is locally free of rank one by that node, so ordinary tensor computes this derived tensor; on trivializations the comparison is $A\otimes_A B=B$, and the transition units reduce to the transition units for $B$. Tensor powers give the assertion for every $r\ge0$; shifts commute with this tensor by [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated]. The shifted Tate line $A_P(r)[2r]$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude, directly from a finite locally free rank-one sheaf and the definition of Tor amplitude [def-kun-tor-amplitude, def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Thus all coefficient comparisons used for it are in the stated domain.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph, first sentence: finite Tate lines and shifts

proof.text:
Here is why the specified map is an isomorphism on $P$, without assuming coefficient compatibility of a chosen purity adjunction. By [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction], identify $\omega_{P,R}$ with $R_P(r)[2r]$ for $R=A,B$, using the counit-compatible comparison of step 3. For the explicit coordinate-tower adjunction in the top-trace node, use that comparison on $D^+$: its representing object $R_P(r)[2r]$ is bounded, and the chosen $\omega_{P,R}$ is bounded by step 2, so the objectwise argument applies. By [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], the counit $\varepsilon_{P,R}$ is an isomorphism; that statement concerns the explicit adjunction, and step 3 carries its counit to the chosen one. Step 2 therefore gives
$$F_{P,B}(u_{P,A,B})=\varepsilon_{P,B}^{-1}(T_{A,B}\varepsilon_{P,A})c_{P,\omega_{P,A}}^{-1},$$
an isomorphism. By step 4, source and target of $u_{P,A,B}$ are shifted copies of the same Tate line. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], after cancelling the shift their morphisms are sheaf morphisms. Since $k$ is algebraically closed and $N$ is prime to $p$, [lem-sc-primitive-root] supplies a primitive $N$th root. The factorization $t^N-1=\prod_{a=0}^{N-1}(t-\zeta^a)$ has pairwise invertible root differences; thus a root on a scheme over $k$ is locally one of these roots (the Lagrange idempotents split the scheme into its root loci). This identifies $\mu_{N,P}$ with the constant cyclic sheaf. Hence this Tate line is a constant free rank-one $B$-sheaf. Its endomorphisms are multiplication by a global section of the constant sheaf $B_P$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant], this section is a Zariski-locally constant function, hence constant on a connected scheme: distinct values would give a partition into nonempty disjoint open-and-closed loci. The scheme $P$ is connected: its coordinate polynomial ring is a domain (leading terms of a product of nonzero polynomials have nonzero product), so its zero prime is a generic point. Hence $u_{P,A,B}$ is multiplication by one $b\in B$. The $B$-linear functor $F_{P,B}$ sends this to multiplication by the same $b$ on $F_{P,B}\omega_{P,B}\cong B_s$, using the top-trace isomorphism. Invertibility of this multiplication implies $b$ is a unit (apply its inverse to $1$). Thus $u_{P,A,B}$ is an isomorphism. For $r=0$, the structure morphism $p:s\to s$ is the identity. Under the counit-compatible identification $\omega_{s,R}\cong R_s$, one has $F_{s,R}=1$ and $\varepsilon_{s,R}=1$. The tensor-unit comparison makes the defining adjunct of $u_{s,A,B}$ equal to $1_{B_s}$; the identity-adjunction Hom bijection therefore gives $u_{s,A,B}=1_{B_s}$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph and third paragraph: verify the canonical affine-space comparison

proof.text:
Choose an affine open chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ from the finite-type affine cover of $X$. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose finitely many $k$-algebra generators $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ of $R$. The surjection $k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\to R$, $t_j\mapsto x_j$, induces a closed immersion $i:U\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf A^r_k$ by the affine characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion]; its composite with $p$ is $a_U$. This is a choice on one affine chart, not a claim that $X$ embeds globally into affine space. The closed immersion is finite, separated and universally closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc], and its affine quotient-ring description makes it of finite type. Thus it is proper, and its compact-support candidate can be taken to have identity open part, so $Ri_!=Ri_*$. Since $i$ is finite, [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] makes its sheaf direct image exact; this also holds for coefficient modules, whose kernels and cokernels have the underlying abelian-sheaf kernels and cokernels. This exactness also identifies the unbounded derived direct image with termwise $i_*$, not just its bounded-below restriction: exactness gives $H^q(i_*L^\bullet)=i_*H^q(L^\bullet)$ for every complex $L^\bullet$, since kernels, images and their quotients are preserved degree by degree. Thus $i_*$ takes every acyclic complex to an acyclic complex and every quasi-isomorphism to a quasi-isomorphism. In the K-injective model of [def-amb-etale-compact-support], the map $i_*L^\bullet\to i_*I^\bullet$ induced by any K-injective resolution $L^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ is therefore a quasi-isomorphism. Hence $Ri_*L=i_*L$ for arbitrary derived inputs, and this exact termwise functor preserves every standard cohomological upper bound. This is the assertion needed for the possibly unbounded-below test object $L$ in the following argument; the bounded-below consequence in the finite-direct-image node alone would not suffice. The ordinary etale closed adjoint is [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. The representing object $Ri_R^!\omega_{P,R}$ is bounded below. In fact, if $\omega_{P,R}\in D^{\ge a}$, then for every $L\in D^{\le a-1}$ one has $\operatorname{Hom}(L,Ri_R^!\omega_{P,R})=\operatorname{Hom}(i_*L,\omega_{P,R})=0$, since exact termwise $i_*$ preserves $D^{\le a-1}$. In the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], take $L=\tau_{\le a-1}Ri_R^!\omega_{P,R}$: the truncation map is zero, while inducing identities on cohomology below $a$, so those cohomology sheaves vanish. The other representing object $\omega_{U,R}$ is bounded by step 2. Hence the objectwise $D^+$ argument of step 3, applied to the composite Hom bijections, gives counit-compatible identifications
$$\omega_{U,R}\cong Ri_R^!\omega_{P,R},\qquad\varepsilon_{U,R}=\varepsilon_{P,R}\circ F_{P,R}(\varepsilon_{i,R}),\quad R=A,B.$$
All the inputs are bounded below; hence the bounded-below compact-support composition statement of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] suffices.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: affine chart, embedding and composition

proof.text:
Set $M=\omega_{P,A}\cong A_P(r)[2r]$, $N=Ri_{A,\mathrm{et}}^!M\cong\omega_{U,A}$, and $M_B=T_{A,B}M$. We first obtain the closed comparison on the ordinary etale site; [lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek] itself is a pro-etale theorem. If $U$ is empty its module derived categories are zero, so the required closed comparison is the unique isomorphism of zero objects; both sides of its counit equation are the unique map from zero to $M_B$ on $P$. Assume henceforth that $U$ is nonempty.

Write $S_{T,R}=\nu_{T,R}^*$, $I_R=Ri_{R,\mathrm{et}}^!$, and $J_R=Ri_{R,\mathrm{proet}}^!$ for $R=A,B$, where $J_R$ is the transported constructible functor of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write $T$ for etale coefficient extension and $T^{\mathrm{pro}}$ for its pro-etale counterpart, with the scheme understood. By [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] comparison is exact and identifies the constant coefficient rings. By [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] $S_{T,R}$ is fully faithful on $D^+$ and its unit $1\to R\nu_{T,R,*}S_{T,R}$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] there are natural $B$-linear identifications
$$t_{T,K}:S_{T,B}(TK)\xrightarrow{\sim}T^{\mathrm{pro}}S_{T,A}K.$$
This is an isomorphism in the derived category of actual $B$-module sheaves. To check its coefficient structure, represent $K$ by a K-flat complex $Q$ with flat $A$-module terms. Then $TK$ is represented by $Q\otimes_A B$, while $S_{T,A}Q$ is K-flat by the cited pullback theorem. Exact comparison identifies $S_{T,B}(Q\otimes_A B)$ with $(S_{T,A}Q)\otimes_A B$ termwise. The balancing maps and their inverses commute with $b\cdot(x\otimes b')=x\otimes bb'$ and with the differential. Hence they are $B$-linear chain isomorphisms and give the displayed comparison before localization. No inference from a mere action on an underlying derived $A$-object is needed.

The identity-open compactification of $i$ is available by step 6. Its dimension is finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], so choose a finite nonnegative integer bound $d$ and apply [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] at both coefficient stages. Its adjunction is relative to bounded-below etale-origin inputs, which suffices here. The defining formula for the finite functor in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], the unit above, and the counit-preserving identification of the ordinary closed adjoint from step 6 give
$$\alpha_{R,H}:S_{U,R}I_RH\xrightarrow{\sim}J_RS_{P,R}H$$
for the bounded inputs $H=M$ at $R=A$ and $H=M_B$ at $R=B$. More explicitly, let $\eta_{R,H}:H\xrightarrow{\sim}R\nu_{P,R,*}S_{P,R}H$ be the specified comparison unit. After identifying the etale compact-support adjoint with $I_R$ by the counit-compatible comparison of step 6, the map $\alpha_{R,H}$ is $S_{U,R}I_R(\eta_{R,H})$, with target $S_{U,R}I_RR\nu_{P,R,*}S_{P,R}H=J_RS_{P,R}H$. Thus it uses the actual functorial transport and its specified unit. Both ordinary representing objects are bounded below: $I_AM=N=\omega_{U,A}$ by step 6, while $I_BM_B\cong I_B\omega_{P,B}=\omega_{U,B}$ by steps 4--6. They are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude by step 2. This does not assume the desired comparison for $I_A$ and $I_B$.

Here is the counit normalization of $\alpha$, explicitly. For bounded-below etale $L$ on $U$ put
$$\delta_{R,L}:S_{P,R}i_{*,R}^{\mathrm{et}}L\xrightarrow{\sim}i_{*,R}^{\mathrm{pro}}S_{U,R}L.$$
Use the explicitly normalized comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], applicable because a closed immersion is quasi-compact and separated (hence quasi-separated). It states that this actual morphism is an isomorphism and that its ordinary inverse-image/direct-image transpose is the pulled-back ordinary etale counit, under the specified inverse-image comparison. It is also the inverse of the compact-support comparison of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] for the identity-open compactification: both are the canonical direct-image comparison with the identity open functor. The comparison-class Hom bijection, at a target $S_{P,R}H$, is the chain
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{pro}}(i_*^{\mathrm{pro}}S_{U,R}L,S_{P,R}H)
&\xrightarrow{\delta_{R,L}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{pro}}(S_{P,R}i_*^{\mathrm{et}}L,S_{P,R}H)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{et}}(i_*^{\mathrm{et}}L,H)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{et}}(L,I_RH)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{pro}}(S_{U,R}L,S_{U,R}I_RH).
\end{aligned}$$
The two site Hom identifications are precisely full faithfulness, using the specified unit. Composing the last Hom group with $\alpha_{R,H}$ gives the relative exceptional Hom bijection for $J_R$. To verify this normalization on an arbitrary morphism, let $f:i_{*,R}^{\mathrm{et}}L\to H$ and let $\widehat f:L\to I_RH$ be its ordinary etale exceptional adjunct. The corresponding pro-etale morphism is $S_{P,R}(f)\circ\delta_{R,L}^{-1}$. After the compact-support comparison, its transpose under $S_{P,R}\dashv R\nu_{P,R,*}$ is
$$R\nu_{P,R,*}(S_{P,R}f)\circ\eta_{R,i_*L}=\eta_{R,H}\circ f,$$
by naturality of the comparison unit. Its etale exceptional adjunct is $I_R(\eta_{R,H})\circ\widehat f$, by naturality of that adjunction. Applying $S_{U,R}$ gives
$$S_{U,R}I_R(\eta_{R,H})\circ S_{U,R}(\widehat f)=\alpha_{R,H}\circ S_{U,R}(\widehat f).$$
This is exactly the image under the displayed Hom chain followed by $\alpha_{R,H}$, so the chain uses the actual transported adjunction, including its counit. All objects in this calculation are bounded below: $L$ is so by hypothesis, $i_*L$ is so by step 6, and $H$ is one of the bounded inputs already specified. At $L=I_RH$, run the displayed chain backwards from $1_{S_{U,R}I_RH}$. Its preimage is the map $i_*^{\mathrm{pro}}S_{U,R}I_RH\xrightarrow{\delta_{R,I_RH}^{-1}}S_{P,R}i_*^{\mathrm{et}}I_RH\xrightarrow{S_{P,R}\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_{R,H}}S_{P,R}H$. On the $J_R$ side the same element is $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{pro}}_{R,S_{P,R}H}\circ i_*^{\mathrm{pro}}(\alpha_{R,H})$, by the defining counit rule for that Hom bijection. Equating these two preimages and precomposing with $\delta_{R,I_RH}$ gives the required exceptional-counit identity:
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{pro}}_{R,S_{P,R}H}\circ i_*^{\mathrm{pro}}(\alpha_{R,H})\circ\delta_{R,I_RH}=S_{P,R}(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_{R,H}).\tag{*}$$

We also identify the coefficient comparison used by the pro-etale theorem. By steps 2 and 6, $N$ is finite-Tor constructible. Thus [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] applies to $i,N$ and supplies its etale comparison $c^{\mathrm{et}}_{i,N}$ and pro-etale comparison $c^{\mathrm{pro}}_{i,S_{U,A}N}$. Its hypothesis that $B$ be finite over $A$ holds because $B$ is a quotient of the finite ring $A$. The two canonical comparisons satisfy the typed square
$$\begin{aligned}
c^{\mathrm{pro}}_{i,S_{U,A}N}\circ T^{\mathrm{pro}}(\delta_{A,N})\circ t_{P,i_*^{\mathrm{et}}N}
={}&i_*^{\mathrm{pro}}(t_{U,N})\circ\delta_{B,TN}\circ S_{P,B}(c^{\mathrm{et}}_{i,N}).\tag{**}
\end{aligned}$$
To verify this square, use [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] to identify $i_{\mathrm{pro}}^*S_{P,R}$ with $S_{U,R}i_{\mathrm{et}}^*$. The canonical direct-image comparison $\delta$ is its mate: its transpose is the pullback of the ordinary etale counit. Each coefficient map is likewise the transpose of that ordinary counit tensored with $B$, by the explicit definition in [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. Here is the common transpose with its source specified. Write $\rho_{R,Q}:i_{\mathrm{pro},R}^*S_{P,R}Q\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{U,R}i_{\mathrm{et},R}^*Q$ for the inverse of the cited pullback comparison, $a_Q^{\mathrm{et}}:i_{\mathrm{et},B}^*TQ\xrightarrow{\sim}T i_{\mathrm{et},A}^*Q$ for tensor-pullback compatibility, and $e_N^{\mathrm{ord}}:i_{\mathrm{et},A}^*i_{*,A}^{\mathrm{et}}N\to N$ for the ordinary (not exceptional) counit. Transposing each side of (**) under $i_{\mathrm{pro},B}^*\dashv i_{*,B}^{\mathrm{pro}}$ gives the map from $i_{\mathrm{pro},B}^*S_{P,B}T i_{*,A}^{\mathrm{et}}N$ to $T^{\mathrm{pro}}S_{U,A}N$ equal to
$$t_{U,N}\circ S_{U,B}(T e_N^{\mathrm{ord}})\circ S_{U,B}(a_{i_{*,A}^{\mathrm{et}}N}^{\mathrm{et}})\circ\rho_{B,T i_{*,A}^{\mathrm{et}}N}.$$
For the right side this follows from the defining transpose of $c^{\mathrm{et}}$ and then that of $\delta_B$. For the left side first use the defining transpose of $c^{\mathrm{pro}}$ and then that of $\delta_A$; naturality of $t$ in $e_N^{\mathrm{ord}}$ gives the displayed expression. The interchange of the pullback/tensor comparisons in this last assertion is the canonical one: on K-flat complexes with flat terms all four inverse-image/tensor composites send a local tensor $x\otimes b$ to the pullback of $x$ tensored with the pullback of $b$, degree by degree. They therefore agree before passing to the derived category, by the K-flat construction in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identify the successive transposes with these composite transposes. Bijectivity of the adjunction proves (**). For the identity-open compactification $c^{\mathrm{et}}_{i,N}$ is also the compact-support coefficient map of [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]: the open tensor factor is the identity and the remaining factor is exactly the ordinary direct-image projection map. No additional coefficient compatibility of an exceptional functor is used in (**).

By [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude], both $S_{P,A}M$ and $S_{U,A}N$ are bounded finite-Tor constructible on the pro-etale site, since $M$ and $N$ have that property on the etale site by steps 2 and 6. The isomorphism $\alpha_{A,M}$ already constructed identifies $J_AS_{P,A}M$ with $S_{U,A}N$; hence the former is finite-Tor constructible as well. In particular the canonical direct-image coefficient maps at both $S_{U,A}N$ and $J_AS_{P,A}M$ are invertible by the pro-etale clause of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. Its naturality applies to $\alpha_{A,M}$: this is a morphism between bounded-below etale-origin objects, and full faithfulness identifies it with a morphism between their etale representatives. This verifies the domains of the inverse coefficient maps and their naturality in the counit descent below, independently of the desired etale closed comparison. All schemes and rings have the hypotheses of [lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek]: $P,U$ are separated finite type over the fixed $k$, $\ell$ is invertible, $i$ is closed, and $A\to B$ is the allowed finite quotient map. Apply that theorem only on its stated pro-etale site, obtaining its counit-defined isomorphism
$$b^{\mathrm{pro}}:T^{\mathrm{pro}}J_AS_{P,A}M\xrightarrow{\sim}J_BT^{\mathrm{pro}}S_{P,A}M.$$
The source and target become the images of the ordinary etale objects $TN$ and $I_BM_B$ via
$$\kappa_1=T^{\mathrm{pro}}(\alpha_{A,M})\circ t_{U,N},\qquad
\kappa_2=J_B(t_{P,M})\circ\alpha_{B,M_B}.$$
The types of these two identifications are
$$\kappa_1:S_{U,B}(TN)\xrightarrow{\sim}T^{\mathrm{pro}}J_AS_{P,A}M,\qquad
\kappa_2:S_{U,B}(I_BM_B)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_BT^{\mathrm{pro}}S_{P,A}M.$$
Each factor is already an isomorphism, without using a coefficient comparison for $I_R$: the inverses are
$$\kappa_1^{-1}=t_{U,N}^{-1}\circ T^{\mathrm{pro}}(\alpha_{A,M}^{-1}),\qquad
\kappa_2^{-1}=\alpha_{B,M_B}^{-1}\circ J_B(t_{P,M}^{-1}).$$
Thus $\kappa_2^{-1}b^{\mathrm{pro}}\kappa_1$ and $\kappa_1^{-1}(b^{\mathrm{pro}})^{-1}\kappa_2$ are mutually inverse arrows between the images of the two specified etale $B$-objects. Here $TN$ is bounded: a finite Tor interval for $N$ bounds its tensor with the degree-zero $A$-module sheaf $B$, and forgetting the $B$ action does not change cohomology. The object $I_BM_B$ is bounded by the earlier identification with $\omega_{U,B}$. Fullness of $S_{U,B}$ on $D^+$ therefore lifts $\kappa_2^{-1}b^{\mathrm{pro}}\kappa_1$ to a unique etale map
$$b_{i,M}:T I_AM\longrightarrow I_BM_B.$$
It is an isomorphism: fullness lifts the inverse as well, and faithfulness identifies both composites with the identities. For clarity, expand the descent of the counit equation. In this calculation put $b=b_{i,M}$, $D_A=\delta_{A,N}$, $D_B=\delta_{B,TN}$, $t_N=t_{U,N}$, $t_M=t_{P,M}$, $t_I=t_{P,i_{*,A}^{\mathrm{et}}N}$, $\alpha_A=\alpha_{A,M}$, $\alpha_B=\alpha_{B,M_B}$, and $c_0=c^{\mathrm{et}}_{i,N}$. Let $E_A$ be the pro-etale exceptional counit at $S_{P,A}M$, let $E_B$ be that at $T^{\mathrm{pro}}S_{P,A}M$, and let $e_A,e_B$ be the etale exceptional counits at $M,M_B$. Write $c_Q^{\mathrm{pro}}$ for the pro-etale direct-image coefficient map at an input $Q$. The defining lifted-map equation is $\kappa_2S_{U,B}(b)=b^{\mathrm{pro}}\kappa_1$. With the indicated coefficient stages understood on each $i_*$, the actual morphisms satisfy
$$\begin{aligned}
 S_{P,B}(e_B\circ i_*b)
 &=t_M^{-1}E_B\circ i_*(\kappa_2S_{U,B}b)\circ D_B\\
 &=t_M^{-1}E_B\circ i_*(b^{\mathrm{pro}}\kappa_1)\circ D_B\\
 &=t_M^{-1}(T^{\mathrm{pro}}E_A)\circ(c_{J_AS_{P,A}M}^{\mathrm{pro}})^{-1}\circ i_*(T^{\mathrm{pro}}\alpha_A)\circ i_*t_N\circ D_B\\
 &=t_M^{-1}T^{\mathrm{pro}}(E_A\circ i_*\alpha_A)\circ(c_{S_{U,A}N}^{\mathrm{pro}})^{-1}\circ i_*t_N\circ D_B\\
 &=t_M^{-1}T^{\mathrm{pro}}(E_A\circ i_*\alpha_A\circ D_A)\circ t_I\circ S_{P,B}(c_0^{-1})\\
 &=t_M^{-1}T^{\mathrm{pro}}(S_{P,A}e_A)\circ t_I\circ S_{P,B}(c_0^{-1})\\
 &=S_{P,B}((T e_A)\circ c_0^{-1}).
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality uses (*) at $B$, naturality of $\delta_B$ in $b$, and counit naturality for $J_B(t_M)$. The second uses the lifted-map equation. The third is the defining exceptional-counit equation for $b^{\mathrm{pro}}$ and the formula for $\kappa_1$. The fourth is naturality of $c^{\mathrm{pro}}$ in $\alpha_A$. The fifth is (**) solved for $(c_{S_{U,A}N}^{\mathrm{pro}})^{-1}i_*t_ND_B$; its right side is $(T^{\mathrm{pro}}D_A)t_I S_{P,B}(c_0^{-1})$. The sixth uses (*) at $A$, and the last is naturality of $t$ in $e_A$.
The first and last lines compare the images of two actual $B$-linear etale arrows in $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(P_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(i_{*,B}^{\mathrm{et}}(TN),M_B)$. Their source is bounded below because $TN$ is bounded and etale closed pushforward is exact by step 6; their target $M_B$ is bounded by step 4. Thus the stated $D^+$ faithfulness of $S_{P,B}$ applies to precisely this Hom set. In the right-hand arrow, $c_0^{-1}$ lands in $T(i_{*,A}^{\mathrm{et}}N)$; this object is bounded below as well, since $c_0$ identifies it with the already bounded $i_{*,B}^{\mathrm{et}}(TN)$. This bound uses the direct-image coefficient theorem at $N$, not any finite Tor dimension of $B$ over $A$. Faithfulness therefore removes $S_{P,B}$. Consequently the lifted isomorphism has exactly the ordinary etale closed counit identity needed below,
$$\varepsilon_{i,B,M_B}\circ i_{*,B}b_{i,M}=(T\varepsilon_{i,A,M})\circ c_{i,N}^{-1}.$$
Thus its etale adjunct is the specified coefficient extension of the etale closed counit. This is the missing site transport at this earlier stage of the proof; it does not use the later dualizing-object realization.

Form
$$v=Ri_B^!(u_{P,A,B})\circ b_{i,M}:T_{A,B}\omega_{U,A}\longrightarrow\omega_{U,B}.$$
The map $b_{i,M}$ is an isomorphism by the full-faithfulness argument above; $u_{P,A,B}$ is an isomorphism by step 5, and the functor $Ri_B^!$ preserves isomorphisms. Hence $v$ is an isomorphism. It remains to identify it with the specified global construction at $U$. Under the composite adjunction, first transpose through $i_*\dashv Ri_B^!$. Naturality of its counit and the counit identity for $b_{i,M}$ give
$$\varepsilon_{i,B}\circ i_*v=u_{P,A,B}\circ(T_{A,B}\varepsilon_{i,A})\circ c_{i,\omega_{U,A}}^{-1}.$$
Here is the final composite-adjunction check with the coefficient factors retained. Abbreviate $F_R=F_{P,R}$, $c_U=c_{a_U,N}$, and $c_{p,Q}=c_{P,A,B,Q}$. The compact-support composition identifications of step 3 give
$$c_U=F_B(c_{i,N})\circ c_{p,i_{*,A}N}.$$
Use $e_A:i_{*,A}N\to M$ and $e_B:i_{*,B}I_BM_B\to M_B$ for the closed exceptional counits from the descent above. After identifying $I_B\omega_{P,B}$ with $\omega_{U,B}$, the closed counit at $\omega_{P,B}$ will be denoted $e'_B$. Naturality of the exceptional counit gives $e'_B\,i_*v=u_P(T e_A)c_{i,N}^{-1}$. Precompose the adjunct of $v$ with $c_U$ and compute
$$\begin{aligned}
(\varepsilon_{U,B}\circ F_{U,B}v)\circ c_U
&=\varepsilon_{P,B}\circ F_B(e'_B\circ i_*v)\circ F_B(c_{i,N})\circ c_{p,i_{*,A}N}\\
&=\varepsilon_{P,B}\circ F_B(u_P)\circ F_B(T e_A)\circ c_{p,i_{*,A}N}\\
&=(T\varepsilon_{P,A})\circ c_{p,M}^{-1}\circ F_B(T e_A)\circ c_{p,i_{*,A}N}\\
&=(T\varepsilon_{P,A})\circ T F_A(e_A)\\
&=T(\varepsilon_{P,A}\circ F_A(e_A))
=T\varepsilon_{U,A}.
\end{aligned}$$
The first line is the composite-counit formula and the normalized coefficient/composition square; the second uses the descended closed-counit identity and cancels $c_{i,N}^{-1}c_{i,N}$. The third is the defining counit equation for $u_P$. The fourth uses naturality $F_B(T e_A)c_{p,i_{*,A}N}=c_{p,M}T F_A(e_A)$, so it takes no inverse of $c_{p,i_{*,A}N}$. The last line is the composite counit from step 6. The only inverse coefficient maps in this calculation are at $N$ and $M$, both independently finite-Tor constructible; $c_U$ is invertible at $N$ too. Cancelling $c_U$ therefore identifies the adjunct with $(T\varepsilon_{U,A})c_U^{-1}$, exactly the defining adjunct of $u_{U,A,B}$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves $v=u_{U,A,B}$; consequently the canonical map is an isomorphism on every affine chart.

proof.text:
For the affine open inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] identifies $j^*\omega_{X,R}$ with $\omega_{U,R}$ for $R=A,B$. Its hypotheses hold: $j$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]; it is separated because its diagonal is an isomorphism. The intersections of its affine source with target affine opens are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], so $j$ is quasi-compact, hence of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. The maps $a_X,a_U$ are compactifiable between Noetherian schemes by step 1. For this open immersion choose the compactification $U\xrightarrow{j}X\xrightarrow{1_X}X$ in [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Its defining functor is $R(1_X)_*Dj_!=Dj_!$, since the identity direct image is the identity on complexes and preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Thus open compact support is exact termwise extension by zero. The open adjunction already stated in [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] is $j_!\dashv j^*$; its Hom bijection sends a map to its restriction on $U$, so its counit is section evaluation. The unique counit-compatible comparison of step 3 identifies any chosen right adjoint with this one. Combining this with the $D^+$ composition comparison of step 3 gives $F_U\cong F_Xj_!$ on the inputs below; thus the subsequent Hom calculation uses the specified open counit. Ordinary inverse image commutes with coefficient tensor by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. These identifications send $j^*u_{X,A,B}$ to $u_{U,A,B}$, as follows from the same counit calculation rather than from any coefficient compatibility of an exceptional functor: the locality isomorphism is the mate of $F_U\cong F_Xj_!$ and $j_!\dashv j^*$. Its counit is $\varepsilon_{U,R}=\varepsilon_{X,R}\circ F_{X,R}(\varepsilon_{j,R})$: the Hom bijections are $\operatorname{Hom}_U(L,j^*a_X^\times N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(j_!L,a_X^\times N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(F_Xj_!L,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(F_UL,N)$, so the counit formula follows by composing them as in step 3. Tensoring commutes with $j_!$: for sheaves the canonical projection map $(j_!P)\otimes M\to j_!(P\otimes j^*M)$ is the identity on stalks in $U$ and $0\to0$ off $U$, by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks]. Tensor commutes with stalks because a stalk is a filtered colimit and tensor preserves colimits. Thus the map is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. If $P$ is a K-flat complex and $M$ is acyclic, exactness of $j^*$ and $j_!$ from the locality node makes $j_!(P\otimes j^*M)$ acyclic. Hence $j_!P$ is K-flat too; the same projection identity computes derived tensor using [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Here is the resulting equality of adjuncts explicitly. Put $W=\omega_{X,A}$, $L=j^*W=\omega_{U,A}$, $G_R=j_{!,R}$, and write $e_R:G_Rj^*\to1$ for the evaluation counit. Let $d_L:T_XG_AL\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BT_UL$ be the tensor comparison just constructed, where $T_X,T_U$ denote coefficient extension on the two schemes. On stalks in $U$ both composites evaluate the same section, and off $U$ both have zero source; therefore
$$e_{B,T_XW}\circ d_L=T_X(e_{A,W}).$$
This identity holds termwise on the K-flat models above and hence in the derived category. All inverses of compact-support coefficient maps below are in their finite-Tor constructible domain. Indeed $L$ is bounded finite-Tor constructible by step 2 and open restriction. Extension by zero keeps its cohomology constructible: extend its finite locally closed stratification from $U$ to $X$, adding the closed complement with the zero sheaf. Its Tor bound is unchanged because the derived projection identity computes tensor with any degree-zero module as $j_!$ of the corresponding tensor on $U$, and $j_!$ is exact [def-kun-tor-amplitude, def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. In particular $G_AL$ and $T_XG_AL\cong G_BT_UL$ are bounded below, so the composition comparison is applicable. By step 3 the coefficient comparison for $a_U$ is
$$c_{U,L}=F_{X,B}(d_L)\circ c_{X,G_AL}.$$
Let $q=j^*u_{X,A,B}$, under the pullback/tensor identification. Its adjunct under $F_{U,B}\dashv a_{U,B}^{\times}$ is, with the composition identifications understood,
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_{U,B}F_{U,B}(q)
&=\varepsilon_{X,B}F_{X,B}(e_{B,\omega_{X,B}}\circ G_Bq)\\
&=\varepsilon_{X,B}F_{X,B}(u_X)F_{X,B}(e_{B,T_XW})\\
&=(T_s\varepsilon_{X,A})c_{X,W}^{-1}F_{X,B}(T_Xe_{A,W})F_{X,B}(d_L)^{-1}\\
&=T_s(\varepsilon_{X,A}\circ F_{X,A}e_{A,W})c_{X,G_AL}^{-1}F_{X,B}(d_L)^{-1}\\
&=(T_s\varepsilon_{U,A})c_{U,L}^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
Here the second line is naturality of $e_B$, the third is the defining identity of step 2 and the stalk evaluation identity, and the fourth is naturality of the compact-support coefficient comparison [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. The last line uses the displayed composition and counit formulas. This is the defining adjunct of $u_U$, so injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives $q=u_U$. This proves that the restriction of the globally defined map is the canonical affine map proved invertible in step 7.

proof.text: Now $u_{X,A,B}$ is an isomorphism. Indeed its restriction to each affine chart is an isomorphism by steps 7 and 8. Restriction to an open is exact, so the kernel and cokernel of every cohomology-sheaf map vanish on the covering. A sheaf vanishing on a covering is zero by the sheaf axiom. Thus these cohomology maps are all isomorphisms, so $u_{X,A,B}$ is a quasi-isomorphism, hence an isomorphism in the derived category. This uses only the definition of cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] and exactness of inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. No morphisms in a derived category are glued, and no equality of global morphisms is inferred merely from local equality.

proof.text:
For the quotient cocycle write $T=T_{A,B}$, $S=T_{B,C}$, $F_R=F_{X,R}$, $c^{AB}=c_{X,A,B}$ and $c^{BC}=c_{X,B,C}$. The input $T\omega_A$ of $c^{BC}$ is in $D^b_{ctf}(X,B)$: step 9 identifies it with $\omega_B$, whose finite-Tor constructibility was proved in step 2. Thus the displayed inverse comparisons all have the domain required by the cited coefficient theorem. To compare $u_{X,A,C}$ and $w=u_{X,B,C}\circ S(u_{X,A,B})$, transpose under $F_C\dashv a_{X,C}^{\times}$. By the defining counit identity at $B,C$, naturality of $c^{BC}$, and the defining identity at $A,B$, respectively, the adjunct of $w$ is
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_C F_C(w)
&=(S\varepsilon_B)(c^{BC}_{\omega_B})^{-1}F_CS(u_{A,B})\\
&=S(\varepsilon_B F_B(u_{A,B}))(c^{BC}_{T\omega_A})^{-1}\\
&=(ST\varepsilon_A)\,S((c^{AB}_{\omega_A})^{-1})(c^{BC}_{T\omega_A})^{-1}\\
&=(T_{A,C}\varepsilon_A)(c^{AC}_{\omega_A})^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is precisely the successive-reduction compatibility in [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change], with the tensor reassociation. The final expression is the defining adjunct of $u_{X,A,C}$, so the maps coincide. With $B=A$, the comparison is the tensor-unit identification and the adjunct is $\varepsilon_A$, whose adjoint is the identity. This proves the quotient cocycle and identity globally, not just chartwise. The counit assertion has already been proved at the moment of construction in step 2.

proof.text:
Finally apply the current finite-stage statement [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] separately with $R=A_{E,n}$ and $R=B=A_{E,m}$. Its hypotheses are exactly the global finite-field datum, $\ell
e p$, these finite DVR quotient rings and the separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$. It supplies $
u_X^*\omega_{X,R}\cong\omega_{X,R,\mathrm{proet}}$, with the latter explicitly defined using the comparison-class transport of the ordinary etale compact-support right adjoint. Thus this application does not require a site-comparison theorem for arbitrary finite rings or an ambient pro-etale adjoint. Applying the derived tensor pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $
u_X$ and the constant ring map $A	o B$ identifies $
u_X^*T_{A,B}\omega_{X,A}$ with $T_{A,B}
u_X^*\omega_{X,A}$. Thus the pullback of $u_{X,A,B}$ gives the asserted isomorphism for the finite pro-etale realization. This is an identification on the constructible, etale-origin objects only: [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] defines the exceptional functor there by transporting the etale adjoint, and [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] identifies its compact-support left functor with the pro-etale one. Consequently the transported Hom bijection sends the transported adjunct to exactly the transported map, and its counit is the image of the etale counit. Pulling back the actual identities in steps 2 and 10 proves the same counit and quotient identities in this realization. No unbounded pro-etale exceptional adjoint or change to a condensed coefficient category has been introduced.
